q: 「核心概念」与具体技术（Redis、Kafka）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between core concepts and specific technologies like Redis or Kafka?
options: 核心概念就是记住产品名（Redis、Kafka 叫什么）
核心概念是技术无关的通用构件，面试处处会用到
核心概念只在学校课堂里出现，工作中用不到
核心概念和具体技术没有区别，学会一个就等于学会另一个
options_en: Core concepts are just the product names, like Redis or Kafka.

Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks — caching, sharding, consistency — that show up in almost every design problem; interviewers assume you know them and will probe once you propose a specific technology.
Core concepts only show up in academic courses, not real work.
There is no difference; learning one technology means you already know the concepts.
why: 核心概念是系统设计的「词汇与语法」：缓存是什么、何时分片、网络如何工作——先有这些才谈得上设计 Instagram。
why_en: Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks that interviewers assume you know and will probe when you propose using them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/流处理平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming and message-queue platform.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    API["APIs"] --> Data["Data model"]
    Data --> Scale["Scaling"]
    Scale --> Consistency["Consistency"]
    Consistency --> Numbers["Numbers"]
optionExplanations: 只背产品名撑不住追问：换成 Kafka 照样答不出该不该分片、要不要缓存。
对，缓存、分片、一致性这些构件跟具体产品无关，换哪家都用得上。
线上系统和面试天天在考这些构件，不是学校才用得到的东西。
会用 Redis 不代表懂缓存原理，换个产品名思路照样断掉。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing product names alone breaks down under follow-ups — swap in Kafka and you still cannot answer whether to shard or cache.
Right — caching, sharding, and consistency are product-agnostic, so they carry over no matter which vendor you name.
These ideas get probed daily in production and interviews alike, not just in a classroom.
Knowing Redis's API is not the same as understanding caching; rename the product and the reasoning falls apart.

scenario: 常规的客户端-服务通信，没有实时推送需求，也没有极端的内部性能要求，要选通信协议。
scenario_en: Routine client-to-service communication has no real-time push need and no extreme internal performance requirement, so you need to choose a protocol.
q: 默认应该选什么？
q_en: For routine client-server communication, what should you choose by default?
options: 自研 UDP 协议
WebSocket
HTTP over TCP
FTP
options_en: A custom protocol built on UDP.
WebSocket.
HTTP over TCP, which is universal, mature, and covers ninety percent of use cases.
FTP.
why: 没有特殊理由就默认 HTTP over TCP：人人都懂、到处能跑；面试官也默认你会这么选。
why_en: Default to HTTP over TCP, which is well understood, works everywhere, and covers ninety percent of use cases.
whenOtherWins: 需要实时推送时才引入 SSE/WebSocket；内部服务间性能关键时用 gRPC。

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，不保证送达和顺序，换来更低开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a transport-layer protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees for lower overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 早期用于文件传输的协议，现代系统间通信很少用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is an older protocol for transferring files, rarely used for modern service communication.

tradeoff: 通用协议覆盖 90% 场景 vs 为特定需求换专用协议的额外收益
optionExplanations: 只有极端延迟场景、且能自己扛丢包和乱序时，自研 UDP 才划算，普通 API 不值得。
客户端和服务端都要频繁主动发消息（聊天、协作）时才上 WebSocket，常规请求响应用不着。
常规客户端-服务通信没有特殊要求时，HTTP over TCP 工具链和团队都现成，默认选它。
FTP 只服务纯文件传输场景，业务 API 不会选它。
optionExplanations_en: Custom UDP only pays off for extreme-latency cases where you're willing to handle loss and reordering yourself — not worth it for a normal API.
WebSocket earns its keep when both sides need to push messages often, like chat or collaboration, not routine calls.
With no special latency or push requirement, HTTP over TCP is the default because tooling and teams already support it everywhere.
FTP is built for file transfer, not the kind of request/response API this scenario needs.

scenario: 系统要给客户端做服务器推送（server push），在 SSE 和 WebSocket 之间选通信方式。
scenario_en: The system needs server push to clients, and you are choosing between SSE and WebSocket.
q: SSE 与 WebSocket 的关键区别是？
q_en: What is the key difference between SSE and WebSocket?
options: SSE 单向推送，WebSocket 双向
SSE 更快
WebSocket 是无状态的
两者完全等价
options_en: SSE is one-way: after the client opens the HTTP connection, only the server pushes down it; WebSocket is truly bidirectional and both sides can send freely.
SSE is faster.
WebSocket is stateless.
The two are completely equivalent.
why: SSE 里客户端无法在同一连接上继续发数据，适合比分/通知这类下行推送；聊天、实时协作这类双向场景要 WebSocket。
why_en: Server-sent events are unidirectional with the server pushing down one HTTP connection, while WebSockets are truly bidirectional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant S as 服务器
    Note over C,S: SSE：单向
    C->>S: HTTP 请求（打开连接）

    Note over C,S: WebSocket：双向
    C->>S: 消息
    S-->>C: 消息
tradeoff: 单向推送的简单性 vs 双向实时通信能力
optionExplanations: 对，SSE 只能服务器往下推；WebSocket 两边都能随时发消息。
速度不是分界线，方向才是——先问谁能发消息，不是谁更快。
正相反，WebSocket 是有状态长连接，要占住服务器资源。
两者一个单向一个双向，能不能双发就区分开了，不是等价协议。
optionExplanations_en: Right — SSE only lets the server push down, while WebSocket lets both sides send anytime.
Speed is not the deciding factor here; direction of communication is.
The opposite is true — WebSocket holds stateful connection resources on the server.
One is one-way and the other two-way, so they cannot be interchangeable.

scenario: 做直播比分 / 站内通知：服务器持续往客户端推数据，客户端不需要频繁往回发。
scenario_en: You are building live scores or in-app notifications: the server keeps pushing updates, and clients rarely send messages back.
q: 更合适的实时方案是？
q_en: For one-way live updates, which real-time approach fits better?
options: WebSocket
SSE，实现更简单
定时整页刷新
gRPC 流
options_en: WebSocket.
Server-sent events, which are simpler to implement and work better with standard HTTP infrastructure.
Full-page polling on a timer.
A gRPC stream.
why: 单向下行推送用 SSE 就够：更简单、能复用标准 HTTP 设施，别为「实时」两个字直接上 WebSocket。
why_en: For one-way server push like live scores or notifications, server-sent events are simpler and fit standard HTTP infrastructure better.
whenOtherWins: 客户端需要频繁上行发数据（聊天、协作编辑）时，才需要 WebSocket 的双向通道。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化，常用于内部服务间调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an RPC framework built on HTTP/2 with binary serialization, commonly used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

tradeoff: 实现简单 + 复用标准 HTTP 设施 vs 双向实时通信能力
optionExplanations: 只有客户端也要频繁上行（聊天、协作编辑）时才值得上 WebSocket 的双向通道。
服务器只需往下推分数或通知时，SSE 用更少的协议复杂度就够，还能复用标准 HTTP 设施。
低频后台数据可以轮询，但直播级更新会浪费延迟和带宽。
gRPC 流适合内部服务间的二进制通信，浏览器通知不走这条路。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket's two-way channel is only worth it when the client also sends frequently, like chat or collaborative editing.
For server-only pushes like live scores, SSE solves it with less protocol complexity and rides on plain HTTP infrastructure.
Polling can work for infrequent updates, but live-level refresh wastes latency and bandwidth.
gRPC streams fit internal binary service calls, not browser-facing notifications.

scenario: SSE/WebSocket 连接要接入生产环境的负载均衡与容量规划。
scenario_en: SSE and WebSocket connections need to run in production behind load balancing and capacity planning.
q: SSE 和 WebSocket 都是有状态连接，这带来的设计后果是？
q_en: What design consequence follows because SSE and WebSocket are stateful connections?
options: 没有影响，照常部署
只能单机部署
必须换成 UDP
不能直接放负载均衡器后面
options_en: No impact, deploy as usual.
It can only run on a single machine.
You must switch to UDP.
You cannot just drop it behind a standard load balancer — you must plan for connection persistence and for a server dying with thousands of active connections.
why: 有状态连接绑定在具体服务器上：LB 策略、连接迁移、宕机时成千上万条连接的重连风暴都要提前设计。
why_en: Both are stateful connections, so you must plan for connection persistence and for a server dying with thousands of active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

optionExplanations: 有状态长连接绑定在具体服务器上，LB 策略、宕机重连都得提前规划，不是照常部署。
多机部署可以做，只是要靠一致性哈希或 sticky session 把连接钉在固定实例上。
换协议不解决连接状态问题，UDP 本身也不管连接归属。
对，得规划连接保持策略，还要预案宕机时成千上万条连接同时重连的风暴。
optionExplanations_en: Stateful long connections tie to one server, so LB routing and reconnect storms need advance planning — it is not business as usual.
Multi-server deployment still works, it just needs sticky routing or consistent hashing to pin each connection to one instance.
Switching transport does not decide which server holds a connection; UDP itself says nothing about that either.
Right — you need a connection-persistence plan and a playbook for a reconnect storm when a server holding thousands of connections dies.

scenario: 内部服务与服务之间的调用，性能关键，接口不对浏览器/外部用户暴露。
scenario_en: Internal service-to-service calls are performance-critical and are not exposed to browsers or external users.
q: 值得提出的通信方案是？
q_en: For performance-critical internal service calls, what communication option is worth mentioning?
options: gRPC——二进制更快
对外 REST 原样复用
SOAP
服务间直接共享同一个数据库读写，跳过 API 调用
options_en: gRPC, with binary serialization over HTTP/2, much faster than JSON over HTTP.
Reuse the public REST API as-is.
SOAP.
Have the services share one database directly and skip the API call.
why: 性能关键的内部通信用 gRPC；常见模式是「对外 REST + 对内 gRPC」。
why_en: Use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication when performance is critical, since binary serialization over HTTP/2 beats JSON over HTTP.
whenOtherWins: 对外公开 API 仍用 REST——浏览器不原生支持 gRPC（gRPC-Web 需要代理且功能不全）。

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化，常用于内部服务间调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an RPC framework built on HTTP/2 with binary serialization, commonly used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 协议的第二代主要版本，支持多路复用等特性，是 gRPC 的传输基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the second major HTTP version with multiplexing support and is the transport gRPC runs on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把资源映射到 URL、用 HTTP 方法操作它们的 API 设计风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that maps resources to URLs and manipulates them with HTTP methods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 XML 信封的老式远程调用协议，企业遗留系统里常见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOAP is an older XML-envelope RPC protocol common in legacy enterprise systems.

tradeoff: 二进制 + HTTP/2 的性能 vs 浏览器原生兼容性
optionExplanations: 内部高 QPS、强类型接口、同团队掌控两端时，gRPC 的二进制序列化比 JSON 更省开销。
对外公开的 REST/JSON 接口是给浏览器和第三方设计的，内部调用没必要照搬这套开销。
SOAP 多见于老系统集成，新建的内部服务基本不会主动选它。
共享数据库会让服务边界消失，一方改表结构另一方就崩，规模一大就很危险。
optionExplanations_en: For high-QPS, strongly typed internal calls under one team's control, gRPC's binary serialization beats JSON's overhead.
The public REST/JSON API is shaped for browsers and third parties; internal calls don't need to carry that overhead.
SOAP mostly shows up in legacy integrations; new internal services rarely pick it on purpose.
Sharing one database erases the service boundary — one team's schema change breaks the other, which gets dangerous at scale.

q: L7 与 L4 负载均衡器的区别是？
q_en: How do L7 and L4 load balancers differ?
options: L4 更智能，L7 更快
L7 懂内容能路由；L4 更快但不看内容
两者完全一样
L4 能读取 HTTP 路径来决定路由到哪个服务
options_en: Layer four is smarter and layer seven is faster.

Layer seven works at the application layer and can route by HTTP content, like sending API calls to one service and pages to another; layer four works at the TCP level, faster but content-blind, just distributing connections.
The two are exactly the same.
Layer four can read the HTTP path to decide which service to route to.
why: L7 看得懂请求内容所以能做内容路由；L4 只管 TCP 连接分发所以更快。WebSocket 这类持久 TCP 连接通常配 L4。
why_en: Layer seven balancers route based on HTTP content while layer four balancers work at the TCP level, faster but content-blind, which suits WebSockets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层负载均衡，能读懂 HTTP 内容按路径/头部路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-seven load balancer reads application content like HTTP paths and headers to route traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层负载均衡，只按 TCP 连接分发，不看内容，速度更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-four load balancer distributes TCP connections without inspecting content, which makes it faster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

tradeoff: 内容感知路由能力 vs 传输层转发速度
optionExplanations: 能力和速度说反了：是 L7 更懂内容，L4 转发更快。
对，L7 能读 HTTP 内容按路径路由；L4 只看连接和端口，所以更快。
两者看到的信息层级不同：一个懂 HTTP，一个只懂 TCP 包。
读 HTTP 路径是 L7 的能力，L4 只转发 TCP 连接，看不到应用层内容。
optionExplanations_en: The capabilities are swapped — L7 is the content-aware one, L4 is the faster one.
Right — L7 reads HTTP content to route by path, while L4 only sees connections and ports, which makes it faster.
They operate at different layers: one understands HTTP, the other only sees TCP packets.
Reading the HTTP path is an L7 capability; L4 just forwards TCP connections without seeing application content.

q: 题目一提「real-time」就上 WebSocket，为什么是常见错误？
q_en: Why is it a common mistake to jump to WebSocket whenever a prompt says real-time?
options: WebSocket 协议已经过时，工程实践里不会再用它
把 real-time 目标当成技术上不可能做到的事
长轮询/SSE 够用时，WebSocket 只是多余复杂度
WebSocket 协议本身不支持任何形式的加密传输
options_en: WebSocket the protocol is obsolete and no longer used in practice.
Treat the real-time target as something technically impossible to achieve.
When long polling or server-sent events would do, WebSocket only adds needless complexity.
WebSocket the protocol has no support for encrypted transport of any kind.
why: WebSocket 的代价是规模化的有状态连接管理；不是「实时」都要它，先问是否真需要客户端频繁上行。
why_en: Proposing WebSockets when long polling or server-sent events would do adds needless stateful-connection complexity at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

optionExplanations: WebSocket 没过时，聊天、协作、多人游戏这些双向场景还是靠它。
real-time 只是延迟目标，不等于必须上双向长连接。
对，只需要下行推送时上 WebSocket，等于白背有状态连接管理和扩容成本。
加密走 TLS/WSS 就能解决，不是弃用 WebSocket 的理由。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket is not obsolete — chat, collaboration, and multiplayer games still rely on it.
Real-time is just a latency target; it does not mean you must have a bidirectional long connection.
Right — reaching for WebSocket when you only need downstream push means carrying stateful-connection and scaling costs for nothing.
Encryption is handled by TLS or WSS; that's not a reason to avoid WebSocket.

scenario: 设计面向全球用户的低延迟系统，服务器在纽约，部分用户在伦敦访问。
scenario_en: You are designing a low-latency global system; servers are in New York, and some users access it from London.
q: 纽约到伦敦的请求，仅光纤中的光速就决定了最低延迟约是？
q_en: For a New York to London request, what latency floor does fiber propagation alone create?
options: ~1ms
RTT 约 70-90ms
options_en: About one millisecond.
A practical round trip of about seventy to ninety milliseconds, with a pure physical floor around sixty.
About two seconds.
About one hundredth of a millisecond.
why: 纽约到伦敦纯物理 RTT 下限约 55-60ms，实践中常在 70-90ms；还没开始处理就有这个级别的跨洋成本，所以全球低延迟必须区域化部署、按地理复制或分区数据。
why_en: A New York to London round trip has a physical lower bound around 55-60ms and practical network latency often around 70-90ms, which is why regional deployments and CDNs exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求从发出到收到响应的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the round-trip time from sending a request to receiving its response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on edge servers close to users.

q: 面试官对 API 设计环节的真实期待是？
q_en: What does an interviewer usually expect from the API-design section?
options: 完美的 API 规范文档
每个字段都定义好类型
跳过 API 直接画架构
端点合理即可，快速推进
options_en: A perfect API specification document.
Every field with its type fully defined.
Skip the API and go straight to the architecture.
Reasonable endpoints so you can move quickly to the harder architecture problems — though sloppy API design signals inexperience.
why: 多数考官不纠结完美 API，他们想看你给出合理端点后把时间留给难点；基本功还是要在，否则显得生疏。
why_en: Most interviewers just want reasonable endpoints so you can move on to harder problems, though sloppy API design signals inexperience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序之间约定好的调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the agreed-upon interface programs use to call each other.

optionExplanations: 正式 OpenAPI 文档是给生产系统写的，面试时间根本不够磨这个。
字段能说清主流程就行，边界字段不用逐个抠。
跳过 API 会让考官看不到你定义的核心对象和主路径。
对，给出合理端点就该往下走，把时间留给存储、扩展、一致性这些难点。
optionExplanations_en: A full OpenAPI spec belongs in production docs — interview time simply does not allow for that polish.
Fields just need to convey the main flow; edge-case fields don't need individual scrutiny.
Skipping the API hides the core objects and main flow the interviewer wants to see.
Right — sketch reasonable endpoints and move on, saving time for storage, scaling, and consistency.

scenario: 面试进行到 API 设计环节，时间有限，要决定投入多少精力。
scenario_en: In the API-design part of an interview, time is limited and you need to decide how deep to go.
q: API 设计环节的合理节奏是？
q_en: What is a reasonable pace for the API-design section?
options: 开场就花 10 分钟反复打磨每一个端点的细节
用 20 分钟把每个端点的全部字段都写清楚
几分钟内画出 4-5 个关键端点然后继续推进
整个 API 设计环节完全跳过，什么都不画
options_en: Spend ten minutes right away polishing every single endpoint's details.
Spend twenty minutes writing out every field for every endpoint.
Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes, then move on.
Skip the whole API-design section entirely and draw nothing.
why: 两三分钟给出 4-5 个关键端点即可；开场 10 分钟还在磨 API 细节说明陷得太深了。
why_en: Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes and move on; ten minutes on API details is going too deep.
diagram:
flowchart LR

用 20 分钟把每个端点的全部字段都写清楚。
几分钟内画出 4-5 个关键端点就继续推进。

q: 分页方式的选择：cursor-based vs offset-based，正确的判断是？
q_en: How should you choose between cursor-based and offset-based pagination?
options: cursor 适合实时插入；offset 够用
offset 永远更好
cursor 无法用 SQL 实现
两者不能混用于同一系统
options_en: Cursor-based pagination works better for real-time data where items are added frequently, while offset-based is fine for most cases.
Offset is always better.
Cursor-based pagination cannot be implemented in SQL.
The two cannot coexist in the same system.
why: 返回大结果集需要分页：数据实时增长时 offset 会漂移，cursor 更稳；一般场景 offset 简单够用。
why_en: Cursor-based pagination works better for real-time data where items are added frequently, while offset-based is fine for most cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条记录的位置作为下一页起点的分页方式，不受新插入影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor-based pagination uses the last item's position as the start of the next page, so new inserts don't shift it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用「跳过前 N 条」定位页码的分页方式，实现简单但新增数据会导致漂移/重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset-based pagination skips the first N rows to find a page; it's simple but drifts when new rows are inserted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

codeSample:
-- cursor-based, stable under inserts
SELECT * FROM posts
WHERE id < :last_id
ORDER BY id DESC
LIMIT 20;
tradeoff: 插入场景下的稳定性 vs 实现的简单程度
optionExplanations: 对，高频插入的列表用 cursor 防漂移；稳定后台表格 offset 简单够用。
offset 在小而稳定的列表能用，高速插入的列表会重复或漏读。
cursor 完全能用 SQL 写：WHERE id < last_id 就是一个稳定范围查询。
同一系统按端点混用没问题，不必把一种分页方式全局化。
optionExplanations_en: Right — use cursors where inserts are frequent to avoid drift, and plain offset where the list is small and stable.
Offset works on small, stable lists, but fast-changing ones can repeat or skip rows under it.
Cursor pagination is plain SQL — `WHERE id < last_id` is a perfectly stable range query.
Mixing pagination styles per endpoint in one system is fine; you don't need to force one style everywhere.

scenario: 系统既有用户登录会话，又有内部服务之间的调用，要给两者选认证方式。
scenario_en: The system has both user login sessions and internal service-to-service calls, so you need auth for each path.
q: 标准搭配是？
q_en: What is the standard auth pairing for user sessions and service-to-service calls?
options: 都用明文密码
都用 IP 白名单
用户会话用 API key、服务间用 JWT
用户会话 JWT，服务间 API key
options_en: Use plaintext passwords for both.
Use IP allowlists for both.
Use an API key for user sessions and a JWT for service-to-service calls.
Use a JWT token for user sessions and an API key for service-to-service calls.
why: 面试口径：JWT 管用户会话、API key 管 service-to-service；点到为止，除非被追问不必展开。
why_en: Use JWT tokens for user sessions and API keys for service-to-service calls.
whenOtherWins: 若有第三方开发者生态，才需要展开 OAuth 之类的授权协议——一般面试不用主动深入。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息编码进一段签名令牌、服务端验签即可信任内容的认证方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes user info so any service can verify it without a database lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 颁发给调用方（通常是服务或第三方）的长期凭证字符串，用于识别调用者身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a long-lived credential string issued to a caller, usually a service, to identify who is calling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 授权协议，让第三方应用在用户同意下访问资源而不拿到密码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OAuth is an authorization protocol that lets a third-party app access resources with user consent, without seeing the password.

tradeoff: 用户会话免查库验签 vs 服务间凭证的可轮换/可吊销
optionExplanations: 明文密码只在本地临时调试能忍，线上认证绝不能这样做。
固定 IP 白名单能当额外防线，但替代不了身份凭证。
把两者用途对调了：JWT 更适合带身份和过期时间的用户会话，不是服务间调用。
对，用户会话要能免查库验签就用 JWT，服务间调用更常用可轮换的 API key 或 mTLS。
optionExplanations_en: Plaintext passwords might survive a local debug session, but production auth can never work that way.
A fixed IP allowlist can be an extra layer, but it never replaces an actual credential.
This swaps the two use cases — JWT fits identity-plus-timeout user sessions, not service-to-service calls.
Right — JWT lets any service verify a user session without a database hit, while API keys give service calls a rotatable credential.

scenario: 你的系统可能被机器人刷接口或恶意滥用打爆。
scenario_en: Your system may be abused by bots or malicious callers that can flood the API.
q: API 层面应该主动提的一句是？
q_en: What API-layer point should you proactively mention for an abuse-prone system?
options: 把 API 下线
提到限流，点到为止
换一种编程语言
禁止所有匿名访问
options_en: Take the API offline.
Mention rate limiting, but don't go deep unless the interviewer asks.
Switch to a different programming language.
Block all anonymous access.
why: 可能被滥用的系统值得提一句限流；分页/认证/限流这些点都是「提到即可」，深挖等考官发起。
why_en: If the system could get hammered by bots or abuse, mention rate limiting but do not go deep unless asked.
whenOtherWins: 纯内部、流量完全可信的系统就不必主动展开限流，把时间留给核心架构。

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内允许的请求数量，防止接口被刷爆或滥用的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate limiting caps how many requests are allowed in a time window to prevent abuse or overload.

tradeoff: 展现生产意识的成本 vs 深挖占用有限的面试时间
optionExplanations: 下线只适合真的无法服务，不是面试里的常规架构答案。
对，接口可能被刷时提一句限流，说明你想到了滥用和下游保护，别深挖占时间。
换语言不改变请求量、配额或滥用风险，这不是相关手段。
全面禁止匿名会砍掉合法的公开读路径，用限流比强制登录更精细。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the service offline only fits an inability to serve at all, not a normal interview architecture answer.
Right — mention rate limiting when abuse is plausible to show you considered it, then move on without a deep dive.
Changing languages doesn't touch request volume, quotas, or abuse risk, so it's unrelated.
Blocking every anonymous request kills legitimate public reads too; rate limiting is the more precise tool.

scenario: 数据是结构化的、关系清晰（用户账户→订单→商品），需要强一致、事务和复杂查询。
scenario_en: The data is structured with clear relationships, such as users to orders to products, and needs transactions and strong consistency.
q: 最合适的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits structured relational data with transactions?
options: MongoDB，文档型数据库，schema 灵活
DynamoDB，键值/宽列数据库，按 key 强项
关系型数据库（如 Postgres），支持事务和复杂查询
S3 对象存储，适合存大文件
options_en: MongoDB, a document store with a flexible schema.
DynamoDB, a key-value/wide-column store strong at key access.
A relational database like Postgres, with transactions and complex queries.
S3 object storage, built for large files.
why: 结构化 + 清晰关系 + 强一致，正是关系型的主场：SQL 表达复杂查询、事务保一致、外键约束护关系。
why_en: Relational databases like Postgres excel with structured data, clear relationships, strong consistency, transactions, and complex SQL queries.
whenOtherWins: schema 频繁变化、或需要不依赖复杂 join 的水平扩展时，NoSQL（DynamoDB/MongoDB）更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with a flexible schema, storing JSON-like documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，用来存文件/二进制大对象，不是给结构化查询用的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service for files and blobs, not built for structured queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制「这个引用必须指向一条真实存在的记录」的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint forces a reference to point to a row that actually exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组操作要么全部成功要么全部回滚的执行单元，保证数据一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a unit of operations that either all succeed or all roll back, keeping data consistent.

tradeoff: 结构化强一致 + 复杂查询 vs 灵活扩展能力
optionExplanations: 文档库适合半结构化数据，但强 join 和事务主路径不是它的强项。
键值/宽列库按 key 高吞吐访问很强，但不擅长跨实体的复杂关系查询。
对，结构清楚、关系多、要强一致时，SQL、事务和外键正是关系型的主场。
对象存储适合大文件二进制数据，不是给订单这类关系查询设计的。
optionExplanations_en: Document stores fit semi-structured data, but heavy joins and transaction-critical paths are not their strength.
Key-value or wide-column stores excel at fast key access, not queries that span relationships across entities.
Right — clear structure, many relationships, and strong consistency are exactly where SQL, transactions, and foreign keys shine.
Object storage is built for large binary files, not for relational queries across orders and users.

scenario: 数据结构频繁变化（schema 灵活），并且要跨多台服务器水平扩展，不依赖复杂 join。
scenario_en: The data shape changes often, must scale horizontally across machines, and does not rely on complex joins.
q: 更匹配的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits flexible schema and horizontal scaling without complex joins?
options: NoSQL（DynamoDB / MongoDB）
单机 Postgres，不做任何扩展准备
强一致的分布式 SQL（如 Spanner），join 成本依旧高
关系型 + 只读副本，schema 变化仍要迁移脚本
options_en: NoSQL, such as DynamoDB or MongoDB.
A single Postgres instance with no scaling plan.
A strongly consistent distributed SQL database like Spanner, where joins still cost the same.
Relational plus read replicas, still needing migration scripts for schema changes.
why: 灵活 schema 与横向扩展是 NoSQL 的两大主场；代价是放弃复杂 join 和部分关系型保证。
why_en: NoSQL databases shine when you need flexible schemas or horizontal scaling across many servers without complex joins.
whenOtherWins: 需要强一致、事务与复杂关系查询时回到关系型——别为扩展性提前放弃这些保证。

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with a flexible schema, storing JSON-like documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

tradeoff: 灵活 schema + 水平扩展 vs 复杂 join / 强一致保证
optionExplanations: 对，schema 常变又要横向扩展、不依赖复杂 join 时，文档或宽列 NoSQL 正合适。
单机不做扩展准备撑不住并发和数据增长，这不是应对扩容需求的方案。
分布式 SQL 保的是强关系和事务，不是为了甩掉 schema 设计成本。
只读副本能扩读不扩写，schema 变化照样要跑迁移脚本。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when schema shifts often and you need horizontal scale without heavy joins, document or wide-column NoSQL fits.
A single instance with no scaling plan can't absorb rising concurrency or data growth; it doesn't answer the scaling need.
Distributed SQL preserves strong relationships and transactions; it's not meant to shed schema-design cost.
Read replicas scale reads, not writes, and schema changes still need migration scripts either way.

q: 「规范化（normalization）」的含义与代价是？
q_en: What does normalization mean, and what does it cost?
options: 把所有数据塞进一张宽表，不做任何拆分
拆表避免重复，读取需要 join
给每个字段单独建一张表来省空间
把重复字段做压缩存储，但仍然保留每处的拷贝
options_en: Put all data into one wide table with no splitting.

Split data across tables to avoid duplication, so orders reference a user ID instead of copying user data: updating once updates everywhere, but reading full data needs joins, which get expensive at scale.
Give every single field its own table to save space.
Compress duplicate fields but still keep a copy in every place.
why: 规范化保一致性（改一次商品名全站生效），代价是读取要 join；表巨大或跨多表 join 时开销显著。
why_en: Normalization splits data across tables to avoid duplication, keeping it consistent but requiring joins that get expensive at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的数据拼在一起返回的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制「这个引用必须指向一条真实存在的记录」的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint forces a reference to point to a row that actually exists.

optionExplanations: 全塞一张表是反规范化的极端，会让重复数据和更新不一致更严重。
对，拆实体表用引用代替拷贝，更新更一致，但读取常常要 join。
每个字段单独成表是过度拆分，查询要 join 太多张表，成本很高。
压缩只省字节，不解决实体关系或重复的事实数据。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming everything into one wide table is the extreme opposite of normalization, and it makes duplication and inconsistent updates worse.
Right — splitting entities and using references instead of copies keeps updates consistent, though reads often need joins.
A table per field is over-splitting; queries end up joining far too many tables and get expensive.
Compression just saves bytes; it doesn't resolve entity relationships or duplicate facts.

q: 反规范化（denormalization）与规范化在「读写」上的取舍是？
q_en: What is the read/write tradeoff between denormalization and normalization?
options: 反规范化会让读和写两条路径都变得更慢
规范化因为省去冗余，读取反而更快
两者在读性能和写性能上其实完全一样
反规范化省 join 换读快，但写要改多处更贵
options_en: Denormalization makes both the read path and the write path slower.
Normalization skips redundancy, so reads end up faster.
The two are actually identical on both read and write performance.
Denormalization skips joins for faster reads, but every write must now update multiple copies.
why: 把 username 直接冗余进订单，展示订单不用再 join users 表；读重、数据少变的系统这笔账通常划算。
why_en: Denormalization duplicates data to avoid joins and speed up reads, at the cost of updating every copy when the source changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据冗余拷贝进多处以省去 join、换取更快读取的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization duplicates data in multiple places to skip joins and speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的数据拼在一起返回的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

tradeoff: 读性能（免 join） vs 写一致性维护成本（改多处）
optionExplanations: 反规范化通常是为了少 join、读更快，不是让两条路径都变慢。
规范化读取常常要 join 多张表，反而不是读得更快的那一边。
读路径要不要 join、更新要改几处，两者的成本形状完全不同。
对，把字段冗余进多处能省 join、读更快，但源数据一变就要改所有拷贝。
optionExplanations_en: Denormalization is usually meant to cut joins and speed reads, not slow down both paths.
Normalized reads often require joining several tables, so it's not actually the faster side for reads.
Whether reads need a join and how many places a write must update — their cost shapes are quite different.
Right — duplicating a field in multiple places skips joins and speeds reads, but every source change must now update every copy.

scenario: 面试中要给数据建模起手式，还没发现任何具体的性能问题。
scenario_en: You are starting data modeling in an interview and have not found a specific performance bottleneck yet.
q: 安全的默认策略是？
q_en: What is the safer default when you start data modeling in an interview?
options: 一上来就全面反规范化
全部数据放进一张宽表
先规范化，按需反规范化热路径
先反规范化冲刺上线，等出现数据不一致问题再回头改规范化
options_en: Denormalize everything from the start.
Put all data into one wide table.
Start with a normalized relational model and denormalize specific hot paths only after identifying read performance issues.
Denormalize first to ship faster, then fix it back to normalized once inconsistency shows up.
why: 别无缘无故上来就反规范化；考官要看的是你懂取舍，而不是盲套技巧。
why_en: Start with a normalized relational model and denormalize specific hot paths only after identifying read performance issues.
whenOtherWins: 如果有明确理由（读极重、数据几乎不变的展示路径），可以更早论证反规范化——关键是给出理由。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据冗余拷贝进多处以省去 join、换取更快读取的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization duplicates data in multiple places to skip joins and speed up reads.

tradeoff: 先保正确性再优化热路径 vs 一步到位追求读性能
optionExplanations: 还没量出读瓶颈就全面反规范化，等于提前替不存在的问题背复杂度。
完全不拆表会让重复和不一致从第一天就存在，不是起步该选的建模方式。
对，先保证正确性和一致更新，再对被证实的热路径做小范围冗余。
先冗余后补救等于先制造一致性问题，再花更大代价往回修。
optionExplanations_en: Going all-in on denormalization before measuring a read bottleneck means paying complexity for a problem you don't have yet.
Skipping table splits entirely bakes in duplication and inconsistency from day one — not a sound starting model.
Right — normalize first for correctness and consistent updates, then denormalize narrowly once a hot path is proven.
Denormalizing first just creates the consistency problem sooner, then costs more to walk back later.

q: 社交 App 用 user_id 做 DynamoDB 分区键（匹配「取用户 X 的全部帖子」），那「查提到 hashtag Y 的帖子」会怎样？
q_en: If DynamoDB is partitioned by user_id for fetching a user posts, what happens when you query posts by hashtag?
options: 要扫描整张表——因为没为这个访问模式设计
自动走索引，很快

q: 最常见的索引结构是什么，强在哪？

布隆过滤器，判断元素可能存在
位图索引，标记低基数字段
全文索引，给关键词搜索分词
options_en: B-tree, keeping data sorted for range queries.
Bloom filter, testing whether an item might exist.
Bitmap index, flagging low-cardinality columns.
Full-text index, tokenizing text for keyword search.
why: B-tree 用有序树同时覆盖「找 email 为 X 的用户」和「查日期 A 到 B 的订单」两类查询，所以成为默认。
why_en: The B-tree keeps data sorted so it supports both exact lookups and range queries, which is why relational databases default to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据有序存放的树形索引结构，同时支持精确查找和范围查询，是关系库默认索引。

位图索引适合低基数字段的分析场景，不是通用 OLTP 的默认选择。

Bitmap indexes fit low-cardinality analytical columns, not the general OLTP default.
A full-text index tokenizes for keyword search; it doesn't support exact ordered ranges.

hash 精确匹配快，但不能范围查询

The two perform identically.

why_en: Hash indexes are faster for exact matches but cannot do range queries, so they are less common than B-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 哈希后直接定位桶位的索引，精确匹配快但无法做范围查询。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据有序存放的树形索引结构，同时支持精确查找和范围查询，是关系库默认索引。

options_en: Write-behind: write to the cache first, then flush to the database asynchronously.

Read-through: the cache layer itself fetches on a miss.
Write-through: writes hit the cache and the database together in sync.
why: cache-aside 实现直白、适配大多数读重系统，是面试默认答案。
why_en: The pattern you will use ninety percent of the time is cache-aside with Redis: check the cache, and on a miss query the database, store with a TTL, and return.
whenOtherWins: 静态资源分发走 CDN、小而少变的配置走进程内缓存——不是所有缓存需求都该进 Redis。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先查缓存，未命中再查库、写回缓存并带 TTL 的缓存读取模式。

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取或重建。

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存、异步再落库的写入模式，写延迟低但有丢数据窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to the cache first and flushes to the database asynchronously, lowering write latency but risking a data-loss window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存层自己负责未命中时去数据库取数据，应用只跟缓存打交道的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-through has the cache layer itself fetch from the database on a miss, so the app only talks to the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同时写缓存和数据库、保持两边同步的写入模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through writes to the cache and the database together, keeping them in sync.

codeSample:

diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> Cache{"Cache hit?"}

    Cache -->|no| DB["DB"]

optionExplanations: write-behind 能吸收写延迟，但异步落库期间有丢数据的窗口期。
对，应用层查缓存、未命中回源查库再回填，实现直白，适配大多数读重系统。

Right — the app checks the cache, falls back to the database on a miss and fills it with a TTL; simple and fits most read-heavy systems.
Read-through moves the fallback logic into the cache layer, simplifying app code but adding system complexity.
Write-through pays an extra cache hop on every write to stay in sync, which raises write latency.

序列化开销太大；策略是换二进制格式
options_en: Not enough memory; the fix is a bigger machine.
Eviction policy is too complex; the fix is to standardize on LRU.
Invalidation: invalidate on writes, use short TTLs and accept staleness, or combine both — the choice depends on how fresh the data needs to be.
Serialization overhead is too high; the fix is to switch to a binary format.
why: 用户改了资料而缓存没更新，下次读就是旧数据；失效策略的选择取决于新鲜度要求。
why_en: The hardest part of caching is invalidation, handled by invalidating on writes, using short TTLs and accepting staleness, or combining both.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry stays valid before it must be refetched or rebuilt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

optionExplanations: 容量不足会拉低命中率，但不是缓存里最容易翻车的取舍。
驱逐策略应对的是空间不够，不解决源数据改了缓存还没更新的问题。
对，数据一更新缓存就可能变旧，写后失效、短 TTL 还是两者结合，看新鲜度容忍度。
序列化会影响性能和兼容性，但通常不是缓存设计里的主要取舍点。
optionExplanations_en: Running low on memory hurts hit rate, but it's not the trickiest tradeoff in caching.
Eviction handles running out of space; it doesn't fix a cache staying stale after the source data changes.
Right — once data updates, the cache can go stale; whether you invalidate on write, use short TTLs, or mix both hinges on how much staleness is tolerable.
Serialization affects performance and compatibility, but it's rarely the central caching tradeoff.

q: 一个热门缓存条目过期的瞬间会发生什么（cache stampede）？
q_en: What happens when a hot cache entry expires all at once?
options: 并发涌向数据库重建（惊群）
缓存自动续期
只有一个请求会去数据库
系统吞吐反而上升
options_en: Many concurrent requests miss at once and pile onto the database to rebuild the entry, a thundering herd that can take down the system.
The cache automatically renews itself.
Only one request will ever reach the database.
System throughput actually goes up.
why: 击穿/惊群是缓存的经典风险：热点 key 一过期，重建流量全部砸到数据库上。
why_en: When a popular cache entry expires, many concurrent requests miss at once and pile onto the database, a thundering herd that can take down the system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热门缓存条目过期瞬间，大量并发请求一起未命中并涌向数据库重建的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede is many concurrent requests missing at once when a hot entry expires, all piling onto the database to rebuild it.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Expire["Hot key expires"] --> Misses["Many misses"]
    Misses --> DB["DB stampede"]
    DB --> Risk["Outage risk"]
optionExplanations: 对，热点 key 一到期，所有并发请求同时未命中，重建流量全砸向数据库。
缓存条目到期后不会自己续期，得有人主动重建或刷新它。
没有加锁或 single-flight 保护时，每个并发请求都会各自去打数据库。
瞬时涌入的重建请求只会拖垮数据库，不会让吞吐变高。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the instant a hot key lapses, every concurrent request misses at once and the rebuild traffic slams the database.
A cache entry doesn't renew itself once its TTL runs out; something has to actively rebuild or refresh it.
Without locking or single-flight protection, every concurrent request goes to the database on its own.
A sudden pile of rebuild requests only drags the database down; it doesn't raise throughput.

q: 防止 cache stampede 的手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which techniques prevent a cache stampede? Select all that apply.
options: 加锁：只让一个请求重建条目，其余等待结果
提前重算：条目过期前主动刷新
错开 TTL：避免大量条目同时过期
把 TTL 全部设为 0
options_en: Locking: let only one request rebuild the entry while the rest wait.
Early recomputation: refresh the entry before it expires.
Staggered TTLs: avoid a mass of entries expiring at once.
Set every TTL to zero.
why: 锁（single flight）、提前刷新、错峰过期是三板斧；TTL 设 0 等于每次都打库，恰恰制造问题。
why_en: Prevent stampedes with locking so one request regenerates, early recomputation before expiry, and staggered TTLs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热门缓存条目过期瞬间，大量并发请求一起未命中并涌向数据库重建的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede is many concurrent requests missing at once when a hot entry expires, all piling onto the database to rebuild it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry stays valid before it must be refetched or rebuilt.

optionExplanations: 只让一个请求去重建、其余排队等结果，挡住了并发重建同时砸向数据库。
在条目真正到期前主动刷新，读请求永远撞不上未命中的窗口期。
把不同 key 的存活时间错开，防止大批条目在同一时刻集体失效。
TTL 设为 0 等于每次都直接打库，制造的正是要防的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Letting only one request rebuild while the rest wait blocks the pile-up of concurrent rebuilds hitting the database.
Refreshing an entry before it actually lapses means reads never hit that miss window at all.
Staggering how long different keys stay alive keeps a big batch of entries from lapsing all at once.
Setting every TTL to zero means every request goes straight to the database — that's the exact problem this is meant to prevent.

q: 与击穿不同的问题：Redis 整个挂掉（full cache outage），防御手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: For a full Redis outage, which defenses keep the database alive? Select all that apply.
options: 小型进程内兜底缓存
熔断器（circuit breaker）卸载负载
优雅降级直到 Redis 恢复
把所有请求原样打到数据库硬抗
options_en: A small in-process fallback cache.
A circuit breaker to shed load.
Graceful degradation until Redis recovers.
Send every request straight to the database and absorb it.
why: 缓存全挂时所有请求都会砸向数据库；进程内兜底、熔断限流、降级是标准防线，硬抗会把库也打死。
why_en: If Redis goes down entirely, defend with a small in-process fallback cache, circuit breakers to shed load, and graceful degradation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测到下游持续失败时主动切断请求、避免连锁故障的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker cuts off requests to a downstream that keeps failing, preventing cascading failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

optionExplanations: Redis 全挂时，进程内的小型兜底缓存仍能接住一部分热 key，减轻瞬时压力。
持续失败时熔断器主动拒绝部分请求，防止数据库被后续流量一起打垮。
关闭非核心功能、只保核心读写路径，把有限容量留给最重要的请求。
没有任何缓冲直接硬抗，数据库大概率也会跟着雪崩，救不了场。
optionExplanations_en: When Redis is entirely down, a small in-process fallback cache still catches some hot keys and eases the immediate spike.
A circuit breaker actively rejects some requests during sustained failures, keeping the database from being overwhelmed too.
Turning off non-core features and keeping only critical read/write paths puts limited capacity where it matters most.
Absorbing every request with no buffer at all usually drags the database down right along with the cache.

q: 「什么都缓存」错在哪？
q_en: What is wrong with caching everything?
options: 缓存越多越好，没有错
缓存变化频繁的数据，白加复杂度
会导致数据库空转
会让命中率达到 100%
options_en: The more you cache, the better, there is nothing wrong with it.
Caching data that changes on every request just adds latency and complexity for nothing — profile first, then cache only frequently read, rarely changing hot paths.
It causes the database to idle.
It pushes the hit rate to one hundred percent.
why: 缓存的适用面是「读多、少变」；对高频变化的数据加缓存纯属负收益。先找热点再下手。
why_en: Cache only data that is read frequently and changes rarely; caching data that changes every request adds latency and complexity for nothing.
optionExplanations: 命中率高不等于选对了目标：缓存热点数据能省钱，缓存易变数据只会拖累系统。
对，请求间几乎不重复的数据放进缓存留不住新鲜度，只多了一层维护成本。
缓存做得好数据库负载会降下来，这是减压而不是空转。
命中率取决于访问模式和淘汰策略，不是缓存范围越大命中率就越高。
optionExplanations_en: A high hit rate doesn't mean you picked the right target: caching hot data pays off, caching volatile data just drags the system down.
Right — data that barely repeats between requests can't stay fresh in cache, so you just bolt on maintenance cost for nothing.
A well-placed cache lowers database load — that's relief from pressure, not idling.
Hit rate depends on access patterns and eviction, not on how much you cache — casting a wider net doesn't raise it.

q: 什么信号说明你可能真的需要分片？（多选）
q_en: Which signals mean you may actually need sharding? Select all that apply.
options: 存储逼近单实例上限（单个 Postgres 到 TB 量级封顶）
写吞吐到顶（数万写/秒）
读吞吐连读副本都扛不住
用户数刚过一万
options_en: Storage nears a single instance's limit, like a Postgres instance capping out in the terabytes.
Write throughput hits its ceiling, tens of thousands of writes per second.
Read throughput that even read replicas cannot handle.
The user count just crossed ten thousand.
why: 分片的三个触发条件：存储、写吞吐、副本也救不了的读吞吐；用户数本身不是理由，要看负载数字。
why_en: Shard when you hit storage limits, write throughput limits, or read throughput that even replicas cannot handle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

optionExplanations: 存储量逼近单实例上限时，再攒数据就会撞到物理容量墙。
写路径吞吐到顶是最常见的真实触发点，垂直扩容和加副本都救不了写瓶颈。
读吞吐连加读副本都扛不住，说明这条扩展路径已经走到头了。
用户数本身不是负载指标，一万用户可能连数据库压力都感觉不到。
optionExplanations_en: Once storage nears a single instance's ceiling, adding more data starts hitting a real capacity wall.
Write throughput hitting its ceiling is the most common real trigger — vertical scaling and replicas can't fix a write bottleneck.
Read throughput that even replicas can't absorb means that scaling path has already run out.
User count alone isn't a load signal; ten thousand users might barely register on the database.

q: 分片时最重要的决策是什么？以 Instagram 为例说明取舍。
q_en: What is the most important sharding decision, and how does Instagram illustrate it?
options: 选数据库品牌
选机房位置
选 shard key
选分片数量
options_en: Choosing the database vendor.
Choosing the data center location.

Choosing the shard key: sharding by user id keeps a user's data on one shard so user-scoped queries are fast, but global queries like trending posts must hit every shard and aggregate, which gets expensive.
Choosing the number of shards.
why: shard key 决定数据怎么分布、什么查询快什么查询贵，牵动整个设计——这是分片的第一决策。
why_en: The shard key is the most important decision: sharding Instagram by user id makes user-scoped queries fast but global queries expensive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片上的字段，牵动整个分片设计的查询快慢分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key decides which shard a row lands on, and it drives which queries end up fast versus expensive across the whole design.

optionExplanations: 换数据库品牌不会影响数据落在哪个分片、哪些查询会变慢。
机房位置影响的是地理延迟，不是分片内部怎么切分数据。
对，shard key 决定了每条数据落在哪个分片，进而决定哪类查询快、哪类查询要付代价。
分片数量是调节参数，真正定生死的是按什么字段切，不是切几份。
optionExplanations_en: Switching database vendors doesn't change how data lands or which queries end up fast or expensive.
Data center location affects geographic latency, not how data gets split across shards internally.
Right — the shard key decides which shard each row lands on, which in turn decides which queries stay cheap and which get costly.
Shard count is a tunable parameter; the field you split on is what actually makes or breaks the design.

q: hash 分片与 range 分片的取舍是？
q_en: What is the tradeoff between hash sharding and range sharding?
options: hash 分布均匀防热点，range 容易局部过热
range 分片的负载分布永远比 hash 更均匀
hash 分片天然就能支持高效的范围扫描
hash 分片和 range 分片在效果上没有任何差别
options_en: Hash sharding spreads load evenly and avoids hot spots; range sharding risks locally overheating.
Range sharding always distributes load more evenly than hash sharding.
Hash sharding naturally supports efficient range scans.
Hash sharding and range sharding produce no difference in effect.
why: 还有目录式分片（查表定位）：灵活但每个请求多一跳依赖和延迟，面试里很少值得提。
why_en: Hash-based sharding distributes evenly and avoids hot spots, while range-based suits naturally partitioned access but risks hot ranges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 取哈希再取模来分配分片的方式，分布均匀、防热点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and takes a modulo to assign a shard, distributing load evenly and avoiding hot spots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 key 的区间连续分配分片的方式，适合天然分区的访问模式但容易局部过热。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns contiguous key ranges to shards, fitting naturally partitioned access but risking hot ranges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一张查找表记录每条数据在哪个分片的方式，灵活但每次请求多一跳依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table to record which shard holds each item, flexible but adding an extra hop of dependency per request.

tradeoff: 分布均匀防热点 vs 保留天然区间局部性
optionExplanations: 对，hash 分布均匀防热点，range 保留区间局部性但容易过热。
时间递增这类写入用 range 反而最容易把最新分片打成热点。
hash 把顺序信息打散了，天然做不了高效的连续范围扫描。
负载均匀度和范围查询能力正是两者区分最大的两个维度。
optionExplanations_en: Right — hashing spreads load evenly and avoids hot spots, while range sharding keeps locality but risks overheating.
Increasing-timestamp writes under range sharding are exactly what overheats the newest shard.
Hashing scrambles ordering, so it can't naturally support efficient contiguous range scans.
Load balance and range-query support are precisely where the two diverge the most.

q: 「10K 写/秒 + 100GB 数据就提议分片」的问题是？
q_en: What is wrong with proposing sharding at 10K writes per second and 100GB of data?
options: 没问题，早分片早安心
分片会降低可用性所以永远不该分
应该先换 NoSQL
过早分片，先做容量数学
options_en: No problem, sharding early means peace of mind.
Sharding lowers availability so it should never be done.
You should switch to NoSQL first.
It's premature — a well-tuned single database with read replicas handles far more than most people think; do the capacity math first and only shard when the numbers demand it.
why: 分片的最大错误是动手太早：10K 写/秒、100GB 离单库上限还很远，提前分片就是无谓地引入巨大复杂度。
why_en: The biggest sharding mistake is doing it too early; at ten thousand writes per second and a hundred gigabytes you do not need it yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

optionExplanations: 这个负载水平离单库真实上限还很远，此时分片只是白背了复杂度。
分片确实有代价，但不是「永远不该做」，量到了真实上限就该分。
换存储类型不解决没做容量测算就动手的问题，方向选错了。
对，先算清单库还能扛多少，再决定要不要分片，别凭数字直觉动手。
optionExplanations_en: This load level is still nowhere near a single instance's real ceiling, so sharding now is needless weight for no benefit.
Sharding does have costs, but 'never shard' is wrong too — once you hit a real ceiling, it's the right call.
Swapping storage types doesn't fix skipping the capacity math first; that's the wrong lever to pull.
Right — work out how much headroom the single database actually has before deciding to shard, instead of acting on gut-feel numbers.

q: 分片引入的新问题有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What new problems does sharding introduce? Select all that apply.
options: 跨分片事务几乎不可能——需要分布式事务或 saga，复杂且慢
热点分片：某个分片流量畸高（Taylor Swift 所在的分片被打爆，其他闲着）
resharding 痛苦：加分片要搬移海量数据
分片后不再需要考虑数据一致性问题
options_en: Cross-shard transactions become nearly impossible, needing distributed transactions or sagas, which are complex and slow.
Hot shards: one shard's traffic spikes far above the rest, like the shard holding Taylor Swift's data getting hammered while others sit idle.
Resharding is painful: adding a shard means moving massive amounts of data.
Sharding means you no longer need to think about data consistency.
why: 分片换来扩展性，同时带来跨片事务、热点、再分片三大痛；设计分片边界时要主动规避跨片操作。
why_en: Sharding makes cross-shard transactions nearly impossible, creates hot spots, and makes resharding a painful mass data migration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一串本地事务加补偿动作模拟跨分片/跨服务事务的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga simulates a cross-shard or cross-service transaction with a sequence of local transactions plus compensating actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个数据库/分片协调、要求要么全部提交要么全部回滚的事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed transaction coordinates commits across multiple databases or shards so they all succeed or all roll back together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分片因为数据/流量倾斜而承受远高于其他分片的负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot shard carries far more load than the others because of skewed data or traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改变分片数量或边界、需要重新搬移数据的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resharding is changing the number or boundaries of shards, which requires moving data around.

optionExplanations: 跨分片边界的写操作没有天然事务保护，得靠慢且复杂的分布式事务或 saga 补。
单个分片被打爆时，扩容别的分片没用，压力全堆在这一个分片上。
改分片数量意味着一次昂贵的数据重分布，不是配置改一下就完事。
分片不但不解决一致性问题，反而让跨片一致性变得更难保证。
optionExplanations_en: Writes that cross shard boundaries lose native transaction protection, needing a slow, complex distributed transaction or saga instead.
When one shard gets slammed, scaling the others does nothing — the pressure sits entirely on that one shard.
Changing the shard count means an expensive mass data migration, not a quick config change.
Sharding doesn't remove consistency problems — it actually makes cross-shard consistency harder to guarantee.

scenario: 面试进行到扩展性讨论，你想引入数据库分片。
scenario_en: In the scalability discussion, you want to introduce database sharding.
q: 正确的话术顺序是？
q_en: What is the right way to explain a sharding proposal in an interview?
options: 直接宣布「我们分 16 个片」
先证明必要性，再给 key 和取舍
说「大厂都分片所以我们也分」
让面试官决定要不要分
options_en: Just announce, "we'll shard into sixteen pieces."
First justify why a single database with read replicas is not enough with capacity math, then state the shard key, and explain the tradeoff of which queries get fast and which get slow.
Say, "big companies all shard, so we should too."
Let the interviewer decide whether to shard.
why: 考官要的就是这条完整逻辑：先证明必要性，再给 key 和 tradeoff；多数面试到这一步就够了。
why_en: Justify why a single database will not work, state your shard key, and explain which queries get fast and which get slow.
whenOtherWins: 容量数学显示单库加副本就能扛时，「不分片」才是正确答案——把复杂度留给真正需要的地方。
tradeoff: 先证明必要性再动手 vs 直接报分片数节省时间
optionExplanations: 没先论证单库到顶就报分片数，会显得过早引入了不必要的复杂度。
对，先用容量数字证明单库不够，再给 shard key，最后说清跨片代价和缓解。
拿大厂做背景可以，但不能替代对本题真实负载的判断。
候选人要主动给出决策和取舍，把选择推给考官等于没答完题。
optionExplanations_en: Announcing a shard count before proving the single database is capped reads as premature complexity.
Right — prove with capacity numbers that one database can't keep up, then give the shard key, then name the cross-shard costs and mitigations.
Citing big-company practice can be background color, but it can't substitute for judging this problem's actual load.
The candidate needs to state the decision and its tradeoff; handing the choice back to the interviewer leaves the question unanswered.

q: 把「Instagram 按 user_id 分片」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the Instagram user_id sharding decision chain in the right order.
steps: 代价：全局查询（全站热门帖）要打所有分片聚合，跨分片事务几乎不可能
需求：写入与存储超出单库上限，读副本也扛不住
缓解：设计分片边界避免跨片事务，全局查询走离线聚合/独立服务
选型：按 user_id 做 hash 分片，用户的帖子/点赞/评论同片
why: 需求（单库到顶）→ 选型（user_id 哈希分片）→ 代价（全局查询贵、跨片事务难）→ 缓解（边界设计 + 离线聚合）。
why_en: Outgrowing one database leads to hashing by user id, which makes global queries expensive, mitigated by shard-boundary design and offline aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片上的字段，牵动整个分片设计的查询快慢分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key decides which shard a row lands on, and it drives which queries end up fast versus expensive across the whole design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 取哈希再取模来分配分片的方式，分布均匀、防热点。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。

对，服务器和 key 都映射进同一个环，顺时针找下一台，增删节点只影响相邻一小段。

why_en: Adding one server to ten means moving about ninety percent of data with modulo hashing but only about ten percent with consistent hashing.

q: CAP 定理的准确表述是？
q_en: What is the accurate statement of the CAP theorem?
options: 三个都能同时拿到
只能同时满足两个；实际是 C vs A
CAP 只描述强一致系统，不适用于最终一致系统
只适用于单机数据库
options_en: All three can be had at once.

You can satisfy only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once; since partitions are unavoidable in distributed systems, the real choice is between consistency and availability.
CAP only describes strongly consistent systems, not eventually consistent ones.
It only applies to single-machine databases.
why: C = 所有节点看到相同数据，A = 每个请求都有响应，P = 网络断裂时系统仍工作；P 是前提，真正的选择题是 C vs A。
why_en: CAP says you can have only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance, and since partitions are unavoidable you really choose between consistency and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络连接在节点间断开时系统仍要能工作的要求，在分布式系统里几乎不可避免要满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partition tolerance requires the system to keep working even when network links between nodes fail, and in practice it's unavoidable.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["Partition happens"] --> Choice{"Choose?"}
    Choice --> C["Consistency: reject stale"]
    Choice --> A["Availability: serve stale"]
optionExplanations: 分布式系统里三者不可能同时全拿到，网络分区一发生就得取舍。
对，分区在分布式系统里几乎不可避免，真正要选的是一致性还是可用性。
CAP 讨论的是分区场景本身，不限定某一种具体的一致性模型。
单机系统不面对网络分区，CAP 讨论的正是多机分布式场景。
optionExplanations_en: In a distributed system you can't hold all three at once; a partition forces a real choice.
Right — partitions are practically unavoidable in distributed systems, so the real choice is consistency versus availability.
CAP is about partition scenarios generally, it isn't scoped to one particular consistency model.
Single-node systems don't face network partitions; CAP is specifically about multi-node distributed systems.

q: 网络分区发生时，「选一致性」和「选可用性」的系统各自表现为？
q_en: During a network partition, how do consistency-first and availability-first systems behave?
options: 两者都直接宕机
两者都继续服务且数据一致
选 C 的系统所有节点数据分歧；选 A 的系统拒绝请求
选 C 拒绝服务；选 A 继续响应会分歧
options_en: Both go straight down.
Both keep serving with consistent data.
A consistency-first system has diverging data on every node; an availability-first system refuses requests.

Consistency-first: some nodes refuse to serve rather than risk returning stale data; availability-first: every node keeps responding, data may diverge temporarily, and it converges once the partition heals.
why: 选 C = 宁可拒绝服务也要数据正确；选 A = 宁可短暂不一致也要有响应。这是分区期间的行为差异。
why_en: A consistency-first system refuses requests rather than serve stale data during a partition, while an availability-first system keeps responding and converges later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

tradeoff: 拒绝请求保正确 vs 继续响应容忍分歧
optionExplanations: 分区时两边至少有一边还在响应，不会同时直接宕机。
分区期间不可能既保证全部一致又保证每个请求都成功，这两个目标互斥。
把 C 和 A 各自的行为说反了，照这个理解后续取舍会全错。
对，C 宁可拒绝部分请求也不给旧数据；A 继续响应，数据可能短暂分歧。
optionExplanations_en: During a partition at least one side keeps responding; they don't both just go dark.
During a partition you can't have every node consistent and every request succeed at the same time — the two goals conflict.
This swaps C and A's actual behaviors, which would send every later tradeoff call the wrong way.
Right — C would rather refuse some requests than serve stale data, while A keeps answering and may briefly diverge.

scenario: 设计社交 feed、推荐系统或分析仪表盘，被问一致性模型怎么选。
scenario_en: You are designing a social feed, recommendation system, or analytics dashboard and need to choose a consistency model.
q: 安全的默认答案是？
q_en: What is the safer default consistency answer for feeds, recommendations, or analytics?
options: 可用性优先，最终一致
全系统强一致
弱一致，不保证收敛
线性一致
options_en: Availability-first with eventual consistency — users tolerate a feed that's two seconds stale, but not an app that won't open.
Strong consistency across the whole system.
Weak consistency, with no convergence guarantee.
Linearizable consistency.
why: 大多数系统默认选可用性：最终一致保证「无新更新时所有节点终将收敛」，对 feed/推荐/分析完全够用。
why_en: For most systems availability is the right default: users tolerate a slightly stale feed but not a down app, so eventual consistency works.
whenOtherWins: 题目一旦涉及钱、库存、订限量资源（订座），就要切到强一致。

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不承诺节点数据会收敛、也不保证顺序的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weak consistency makes no guarantee that replicas will ever converge or that updates are seen in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最严格的一致性模型，所有操作看起来像按一个全局顺序瞬时发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability is the strictest consistency model, making all operations appear to happen instantly in one global order.

tradeoff: 可用性默认（最终一致） vs 强一致带来的协调延迟
optionExplanations: 对，用户能忍 feed 慢几秒，但忍不了打不开的 App，最终一致对这些场景够用。
全系统都上强一致会付出协调延迟和可用性下降的代价，feed/推荐用不上这么重。
弱一致连收敛都不承诺，展示型数据也很难接受这么松的保证。
线性一致是最严格的模型，代价最高，留给真的需要防超卖的路径。
optionExplanations_en: Right — users tolerate a feed that's a few seconds stale far more than an app that won't load, so eventual consistency is enough here.
Strong consistency everywhere pays a coordination-latency and availability cost that feeds or recommendations don't need.
Weak consistency doesn't even promise convergence, which is too loose even for display-only data.
Linearizability is the strictest, costliest model, best reserved for paths that truly must prevent overselling.

scenario: 库存计数、银行账户余额、Ticketmaster 座位预订——读到几秒前的旧数据就会超卖 / 放过欺诈 / 重复订座。
scenario_en: Inventory counts, bank balances, or ticket seats can oversell, allow fraud, or double-book if reads are stale by a few seconds.
q: 一致性模型该选？
q_en: Which consistency model should you choose for stale-read-sensitive paths?
options: 最终一致
弱一致
强一致（防超卖）
不需要一致性
options_en: Eventual consistency.
Weak consistency.
Strong consistency, because stale data causes real financial loss.
No consistency guarantee needed.
why: 强一致的适用判据是「陈旧读会造成实际业务损失」；同一应用可混用：电商的商品描述/评论最终一致、库存/下单强一致。
why_en: Choose strong consistency when stale reads cause real business harm, like overselling inventory, fraud, or double-booked seats.
whenOtherWins: 同系统里的展示型数据（描述、评论晚 5 秒出现没人在乎）继续用最终一致即可。

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

tradeoff: 数据实时正确（防超卖/防欺诈） vs 协调延迟和可用性下降
optionExplanations: 最终一致允许短暂旧读，库存/余额场景陈旧几秒就可能超卖或错扣钱。
弱一致连收敛都不保证，对这类会造成实际损失的路径风险更大。
对，读到几秒前的旧数据会超卖、放过欺诈、重复订座，这类路径必须强一致。
库存、余额、订座这类共享可变状态离不开一致性保证，不可能不管。
optionExplanations_en: Eventual consistency allows brief stale reads, and a few stale seconds on inventory or balance can already cause overselling or a wrong charge.
Weak consistency doesn't even guarantee convergence, which is riskier still on paths where staleness causes real loss.
Right — reading a few-seconds-old value here can oversell inventory, miss fraud, or double-book a seat, so these paths need strong consistency.
Shared mutable state like inventory, balances, or seat bookings can't skip a consistency guarantee altogether.

q: 最终一致（eventual）与弱一致（weak）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between eventual consistency and weak consistency?

两者是同义词
弱一致更强
最终一致等于强一致
options_en: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes eventually converge to the same state; weak consistency makes no such convergence guarantee.
The two are synonyms.
Weak consistency is the stronger guarantee.
Eventual consistency is the same as strong consistency.
why: 「最终」是一个有内容的承诺——会收敛；弱一致什么都不承诺。面试别把两个词混用。
why_en: Eventual consistency guarantees all nodes converge given enough time without updates, while weak consistency makes no convergence guarantee at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不承诺节点数据会收敛、也不保证顺序的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weak consistency makes no guarantee that replicas will ever converge or that updates are seen in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

tradeoff: 承诺最终收敛 vs 不承诺任何收敛
optionExplanations: 对，最终一致至少承诺没有新写入后会收敛；弱一致什么都不保证。
两个词面试里混用会丢掉「会不会收敛」这个关键差别，不是同义词。
弱一致的保证比最终一致更少，不是更强的那一边。
强一致要求随时读到最新写入，比最终一致的收敛承诺严格得多。
optionExplanations_en: Right — eventual consistency at least promises convergence once new writes stop; weak consistency promises nothing.
Conflating the two terms in an interview loses the key difference of whether convergence is guaranteed at all.
Weak consistency actually guarantees less than eventual, not more.
Strong consistency requires reading the latest write at all times, a much stricter bar than eventual's convergence promise.

q: PACELC 定理补充了 CAP 的什么盲区？
q_en: What blind spot in CAP does PACELC cover?
options: 网络分区发生时，PACELC 建议直接选延迟
CAP 定理其实只适用于单机部署的数据库
在实际系统里网络分区永远不会真的发生
日常运行里其实是一致性和延迟的取舍
options_en: When a partition happens, PACELC says just choose latency.
CAP theorem actually only applies to single-machine databases.
In real systems, network partitions never actually happen.
Day to day, the real tradeoff is between consistency and latency.
why: PACELC：分区（P）时选 A 或 C；否则（E）选延迟（L）或一致性（C）。日常运行中强一致的代价是协调延迟。
why_en: PACELC notes that outside rare partitions the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency, since strong consistency requires coordination before responding.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 的补充：分区时选可用性或一致性，其他时候（日常）选延迟或一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PACELC extends CAP: during a Partition choose Availability or Consistency, Else choose Latency or Consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

optionExplanations: 分区时 PACELC 谈的仍是可用性还是一致性，延迟选项出现在没分区的日常运行里。
CAP 本身讨论的就是多机分布式场景，不是单机适用范围的问题。
分区当然会发生，PACELC 正是为了补上「平时」这个 CAP 没讲的部分。
对，CAP 只讲分区这种少见时刻，日常运行里真正的取舍是一致性和延迟。
optionExplanations_en: During a partition PACELC is still about availability versus consistency; latency enters the picture during normal operation.
CAP is already about multi-node distributed scenarios, not a question of single-machine scope.
Partitions certainly do happen; PACELC exists precisely to cover the everyday case CAP leaves out.
Right — CAP only covers the rare partition moment, while day to day the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency.

q: 把「订票系统选强一致」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the strong-consistency decision chain for a ticket-booking system in the right order.
steps: 选型：对这些关键路径选择强一致
需求：库存/余额/订座——读到陈旧数据会超卖、放过欺诈或重复订座
缓解：只对关键路径强一致，描述、评论等展示数据用最终一致
代价：分区时部分请求被拒，且日常延迟更高（节点需先协调）
why: 需求（陈旧读有真实代价）→ 选强一致 → 代价（可用性与延迟）→ 缓解（按路径混用一致性模型）。
why_en: Stale reads costing real money lead to strong consistency, whose availability and latency costs are contained by applying it only to critical paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Loss["Stale read causes loss"] --> Strong["Strong consistency"]
    Strong --> Cost["Higher latency / lower availability"]
    Cost --> Mix["Use only on critical path"]
tradeoff: 关键路径强一致防超卖 vs 非关键路径最终一致保可用性/延迟

q: 脑子里装着 2010 年代的硬件数字做设计，会导致什么？
q_en: What happens if you design with outdated 2010s hardware numbers in mind?
options: 设计更保守更安全
过早提出分片和缓存
没有影响
面试官会觉得你经验老到
options_en: The design becomes more conservative and safer.
You propose sharding and caching far earlier than necessary — a modern tuned database handles tens of thousands of QPS, and a single Redis handles hundreds of thousands of ops per second.
It has no effect.
The interviewer will think you're seasoned.
why: 现代硬件比多数候选人以为的强得多；用老数字就会为不存在的瓶颈加复杂度。
why_en: Using 2010-era numbers makes you propose sharding and caching far earlier than needed, since modern servers handle tens of thousands of queries per second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统每秒处理的查询数，常用来估算需要多少台服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is the number of queries a system handles per second, often used to estimate how many servers you need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

optionExplanations: 保守不等于正确，为不存在的瓶颈加复杂度是过度设计，不是更安全。
对，现代硬件比老数字强得多，用旧认知就会为不存在的瓶颈提前加复杂度。
用错年代的硬件数字直接决定了你在哪个负载点开始提分片，影响很实在。
老数字暴露的是认知过时，考官更可能觉得你没跟上现代硬件的进展。
optionExplanations_en: Conservative doesn't mean correct; adding complexity for a bottleneck that doesn't exist is over-engineering, not safety.
Right — modern hardware is far stronger than those old numbers suggest, so outdated assumptions trigger sharding and caching too soon.
Which hardware era you assume directly shifts the load point where you start proposing sharding, so the effect is real.
Outdated numbers signal you haven't kept up, which reads as less experienced, not more seasoned.

q: 补全延迟阶梯（影响几乎所有设计决策）：
q_en: Fill in the latency ladder that shapes almost every design decision.
text: 内存访问约{{纳秒}}级；SSD 读取约{{微秒}}级；数据中心内网络调用约 {{1-10}} 毫秒；跨大洲调用要几十到几百毫秒。

scenario: 数据量还在增长，团队在纠结现在要不要把 Postgres 拆分片。

q_en: Roughly how much storage can one Postgres instance comfortably hold, and when should sharding enter the conversation?
options: 舒适到几个 TB；分片门槛更高
只能存 10GB
1TB 就必须分片
存储无上限
options_en: A few terabytes comfortably; sharding is needed only in the tens to hundreds of terabytes — proposing it at 500GB is needless complexity.
Only 10GB.
Sharding is mandatory at 1TB.
Storage has no upper limit.
why: 存储容量是分片决策的核心数字之一；数据量远低于单库上限时提出分片会被视为乱加复杂度。
why_en: A single Postgres handles a few terabytes comfortably, so you do not need sharding until tens or hundreds of terabytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储容量单位，1 TiB ≈ 1024 GB，用来衡量单库存储上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB (tebibyte) is a storage unit of about 1024 GB, used to gauge a single database's storage ceiling.

optionExplanations: 对，单实例能舒服存到几个 TB，真要分片通常是几十上百 TB 才谈得上。
10GB 远低于单实例的真实上限，按这个数字规划会严重低估容量。
1TB 离单实例真实上限还差得远，这个门槛定得太保守了。
存储终究要落盘，单实例硬件和文件系统都有真实容量上限。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a single instance handles a few terabytes comfortably; sharding usually only enters the picture in the tens or hundreds of terabytes.
Ten gigabytes is far below a single instance's real ceiling; planning around that number badly underestimates capacity.
One terabyte is still well short of a single instance's real ceiling, so that threshold is set too conservatively.
Storage still lands on real disks; a single instance's hardware and filesystem both have an actual ceiling.

scenario: 要判断单个数据库实例还能不能撑住业务增长，什么信号说明该扩容了。
scenario_en: You need to decide whether one database instance can keep handling growth, and which signals trigger expansion.
q: 数据库的关键量级与扩容触发点（记忆锚点）是？
q_en: What database scale anchors and expansion triggers should you remember?
options: 最多 100 TPS，10GB 存储
约 5 万 TPS；触发点看写吞吐/延迟
无限 TPS
1000 TPS 就必须分库
options_en: At most 100 TPS and 10GB of storage.

Up to about fifty thousand TPS, sub-five-millisecond cached reads, and 64 TiB-plus storage; consider action when writes pass ten thousand TPS, uncached reads exceed five milliseconds, or you need geographic distribution.
Unlimited TPS.
You must shard at 1000 TPS.
why: 这组数字回答「单库还能不能扛」；没超过触发点就别急着分片或换存储。
why_en: A database handles up to about fifty thousand transactions per second with sub-five-millisecond cached reads, with scale triggers at ten thousand write TPS or slow uncached reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库每秒能处理的事务数，是判断单库还能不能扛的核心指标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS is the number of transactions a database can process per second, a key signal for whether a single instance can still keep up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储容量单位，1 TiB ≈ 1024 GB，用来衡量单库存储上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB (tebibyte) is a storage unit of about 1024 GB, used to gauge a single database's storage ceiling.

optionExplanations: 100 TPS 严重低估了现代调优过的数据库实力，会让人过早焦虑扩容。
对，单库能撑到近 5 万 TPS，真正该看的信号是写吞吐或未命中延迟是否顶到触发点。
硬件、连接数、锁竞争都有真实上限，不存在无限吞吐这回事。
1000 TPS 离单库真实上限还差得远，这个门槛定得太低了。
optionExplanations_en: One hundred TPS badly underestimates a modern tuned database, and it triggers scaling worries far too early.
Right — a single instance can handle close to fifty thousand TPS; the real signal to watch is write throughput or uncached latency hitting the trigger point.
Hardware, connection limits, and lock contention all cap throughput; there's no such thing as unlimited TPS.
One thousand TPS is still well below a single instance's real ceiling, so that threshold is set far too low.

scenario: 线上 Redis 集群做容量规划，要知道什么信号说明该扩容或优化。
scenario_en: You are capacity-planning a Redis cluster and need signals for expansion or optimization.
q: 缓存（Redis 级别）的关键量级与告警触发点是？
q_en: What Redis-scale cache anchors and alert triggers should you remember?
options: 延迟 100ms、1k ops/s
延迟 1 秒、10k ops/s
~1ms、10万+ ops/s
没有任何上限
options_en: 100ms latency, 1k ops per second.
1 second latency, 10k ops per second.
About 1ms latency, over 100k ops per second, memory up to about 1TB; watch for hit rate below eighty percent, latency above one millisecond, or memory above eighty percent.
No upper limit at all.
why: 用这组数字判断「单个缓存实例够不够」以及何时该扩缓存集群。
why_en: A cache serves in about a millisecond at over a hundred thousand operations per second up to about a terabyte of memory, with hit rate below eighty percent as a key trigger.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

optionExplanations: 100ms、1k ops/s 完全低估了内存型缓存的真实速度，会误导容量判断。
1 秒延迟更是离谱地慢，Redis 这类内存缓存不会是这个数量级。
对，Redis 单实例常在约 1ms、10 万+ ops/s 运转，命中率或内存过高才是该扩容的信号。
内存容量和单机网络吞吐都有硬上限，不存在完全无上限的缓存节点。
optionExplanations_en: 100ms latency and 1k ops per second badly underestimate an in-memory cache's real speed, which would mislead capacity planning.
One second of latency is even more implausible — an in-memory cache like Redis never runs that slow.
Right — a single Redis instance typically runs around one millisecond and over a hundred thousand ops per second; a falling hit rate or high memory use is the real scale-up signal.
Memory capacity and single-node network throughput both have hard ceilings; no cache node is truly limitless.

scenario: 消息队列（如 Kafka）做容量规划，要知道什么信号说明该给 broker 扩容。

每秒 1 万条是极限
端到端延迟至少 1 秒
单 broker ~100万条/秒
options_en: One hundred messages per second per broker.
Ten thousand per second is the ceiling.
At least one second of end-to-end latency.

Ten thousand per second is still far short of a single broker's real ceiling; treating it as the limit triggers scaling far too early.

Right — a single broker can reach about a million messages per second; the real signals are approaching that ceiling or growing consumer lag.
